newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas untraded for first time since June 18.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas untraded for first time since June 18.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures activity did not pick up on Monday afternoon after a blank morning session, and no trade was done over the day for the first time in nearly three weeks.

Although volumes have been generally thin in recent weeks, there have been at least 50 lots done each day since 18 June, the last day on which no trade was done at all. The highest volume since then was on June 25, when 180 lots were done.
Last week 365 lots were traded, at an average of 73 lots a day.

Bids and offers straddled the previous settlement level by the close of the afternoon session on Monday, an indication that there was no clear price direction. Front month August was bid at 9.30 pence a therm at the close, against an offer at 9.70 pence. August had settled at 9.415 pence on Friday.
And March 1998, the last month to see both a bid and an offer posted by the close on Monday, saw a gap of 0.75 pence a therm between the two.
Only seven of the 12 contract months saw both bids and offers by the 1500 GMT close of the afternoon session.
A physical trader said the OTC market had been slightly softer, but little activity was seen and market fundamentals had remained unchanged on a quiet Monday.
